A write-ahead log is a file that contains a record of all changes made to the database. When a change is made to the database, the change is first written to the log, and then the change is written to the database itself. This ensures that the log always contains a complete and accurate record of all changes made to the database, even if the database itself is corrupted or lost.
When a database crashes, the log can be used to recover the database to a consistent state. The database can be restored to a point in time just before the crash by replaying all the changes recorded in the log up to that point. This ensures that the database is consistent and up-to-date, even if some changes were not fully written to the database before the crash.
The log can also be used to recover from a situation where the database is inconsistent, such as when a transaction is partially committed. In this case, the log can be used to determine which transactions were partially committed and which ones were not, and the database can be restored to a consistent state by rolling back the partially committed transactions.
